source.title: A study on the plasticity of neural networks
source.authors: Tudor Berariu; W. Czarnecki; Soham De; Jörg Bornschein; Samuel L. Smith; Razvan Pascanu; C. Clopath

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; figure values are not transcribed, and several results are available only as plots.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how pretraining on data from the same distribution changes later test performance versus fresh initialization. This is a related generalization-gap question, but it does not test the specific behaviors named by V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization, interpolation-threshold widening, convolutional versus fully connected performance, adaptive-optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. It reports its own warm-start results; cited findings about other mechanisms are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether same-distribution pretraining reduces subsequent generalization relative to fresh initialization. Its results do not test the behaviors or comparisons specified by V1–V8. Discussion of architecture, sharpness and batch-induced noise supplies context and hypotheses rather than direct tests.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors extend evidence that same-distribution pretraining can impair subsequent generalization across optimizer, distribution-transition, stage-count and model-capacity settings. Resetting upper layers or increasing the tuning learning rate can alleviate the penalty. Reduced gradient noise and weaker exploration are proposed explanations requiring further evidence, rather than measured mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines warm-start versus fresh-initialization performance on CIFAR-10, rather than the interventions or measurements in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported gap varies with pretraining duration, number and distributional discrepancy of stages, model width and depth, which layers are reset, optimizer, and tuning learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-distribution pretraining reduces subsequent test accuracy relative to fresh initialization despite both reaching full training accuracy; the penalty occurs with all four tested optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Warm-starting can impair subsequent generalization even when training error reaches zero.

fits_no_version.finding: The penalty appears after few pretraining epochs, persists with smooth distribution transitions, and grows with additional stages or greater distribution discrepancies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transient sampling history can affect final generalization after training on the full dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing residual-network depth and width does not eliminate the warm-start penalty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater model capacity does not necessarily restore fresh-initialization performance after pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: Resetting upper layer groups can recover fresh-model performance, while a tenfold larger tuning learning rate substantially reduces the penalty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer reinitialization and tuning learning rate can alleviate warm-start generalization loss.

record.problems: Most results are shown only in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. Experiments use CIFAR-10 and ResNet-18 except the architecture sweep; the proposed gradient-noise explanation is described as a hypothesis requiring further empirical evidence.
record.rows_left_out: No results relevant to V1–V8 were reported. Cited prior-work findings, including sharpness and regularization claims discussed in Section 3 and Appendix B, were not extracted as this study's own results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training under the same recipe.
Whether widening beyond the width required for zero training error continues lowering test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning regimes and proposed remedies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that alleviate them.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps and its ranking against other measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples compared with equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because the rows measure a different effect; this does not dispute the reported warm-start findings. The paper's generalization gap means pretrained versus freshly initialized test performance, whereas V7 concerns the training–test error gap.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label comparison of the same recipe.
Width and depth are varied in a warm-start comparison, but the study does not test widening past the interpolation threshold for the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
The paper compares the warm-start gap across optimizers, not adaptive optimizers against SGD for held-out performance.
Sharpness and the specified magnitude-aware measure are not measured.
Memorized examples are not identified, removed, or compared with random removals.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained on half of CIFAR-10 training data, then tuned on the full training set; compared with training from scratch.

conditions.value: 350 epochs on half of training data
average test accuracy in last 100 epochs

rows.uncertainty: Figure states error bars measure standard deviation; values not transcribed.
rows.note: Authors state that the pretrained model generalizes worse than the model trained from scratch; both stages reach 100% accuracy on their training data.
rows.check: The stated warm-start penalty is supported, but it measures no claim version. Fitting natural labels to zero training error does not test random-label memorization in V1.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared warm-start generalization with fresh initialization using different optimizers.

conditions.value: Adam, RMSprop, SGD, SGD with momentum

rows.value: gap manifests for all considered optimizers
rows.note: The text says the gap manifests in all cases; optimizer-specific plot values are not available in the supplied text.
rows.check: This measures the warm-start penalty within each optimizer. It does not establish adaptive optimizers' performance relative to learning-rate-tuned SGD as specified in V4. The reported gap is a warm-start versus fresh-initialization difference.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of pretraining epochs before tuning.
rows.measure: Average test accuracy in last 100 tuning epochs
rows.uncertainty: Figure shows average and one-seed curves; numerical uncertainty not stated in text.
rows.note: Text says more pretraining steps hurt tuning generalization and that 5–10 epochs are enough to observe a gap.
rows.check: Pretraining duration affects the warm-start penalty, which no version names. The text establishes the direction despite unavailable numerical plot values.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained in a single stage with examples sampled between the pretraining subset and full training data.

conditions.value: smooth sampling transition controlled by γ

rows.baseline: no-pretraining and pretrained references; figure only
rows.note: Authors state that the gap manifests even for a small number of epochs with biased sampling.
rows.check: Biased sampling followed by a smooth distribution transition measures a warm-start effect, not any version's intervention.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained in multiple stages with data splits, then tuned on the full training set.
rows.uncertainty: Figure shows averages and one-seed curves; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: Text says final generalization performance degrades with number of splits and higher discrepancies between stages lead to worse generalization.
rows.check: Stage count and class imbalance affect final generalization, but neither tests V1–V8.

rows.subject: Residual networks of various depths and widths
rows.size_stated: widths and depths varied; exact plotted values not transcribed
rows.operation_detail: Varied residual-network width and depth and compared pretrained with fresh initialization.

conditions.value: ResNet-18 modified in module depth and channel width

rows.note: Text states that even very deep and wide models retain a significant gap between pretrained and randomly initialized models.
rows.check: The residual-network capacity sweep establishes persistence of the warm-start penalty. It does not establish test-error behavior beyond a measured interpolation threshold as required by V2.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Reset selected layers after pretraining, then tuned.
rows.uncertainty: Figure shows averages and one-seed curves; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: Text says resetting a small subset is not enough to fully recover the gap; reinitializing the top part is needed. Resetting the last 4 or 5 modules seems to recover original performance.
rows.check: Resetting pretrained layers tests recovery from the warm-start penalty, not a listed version. Appendix A.5 supports recovery after resetting the last four or five indexed layer groups.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared tuning after pretraining under different constant learning rates with fresh training.

conditions.value: varied; plotted values not fully recoverable

rows.uncertainty: Each point is the average of 9 seeds; error measure not stated.
rows.note: Authors state that a 10x larger learning rate reduces the gap substantially; further empirical evidence is required to validate the proposed hypothesis.
rows.check: Learning-rate changes reduce the warm-start penalty. This neither measures magnitude-aware sharpness for V7 nor compares adaptive optimizers with SGD for V4. Appendix A specifies standard-deviation error bars for all plots.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
